To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new cyanide-bridge coordination polymer constructed from [Cu(II)2Ni(II)(II)(CN)8(H2O)4]·H2 O has been synthesized and structurally characterized.
a novel two-dimensional cyanide-bridging Cu(II)- Ni(II) heteronuclear coordination polymer, {[Cu(II)(CN4)Ni(II)]·H2O}, has been synthesized and structurally characterized.

a new two-dimensional grid-like heterometallic Cu-Ni coordination polymer, poly[[diaquaterakis-μ2-cyano-κ(8)-C:N-nickell(II)copper-(II)] monohydrate], {[Cu(2+)Ni(CN)2(H2O)4]·H2)O}n, with the presence of interlayer O--H...N and intramolecular O--H...O hydrogen bonds has been synthesized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and magnetic properties of a new cyanide-bridge heterometallic complex, which has a two-dimensional network structure.
the synthesis and characterization of new coordination polymers with a cyanide bridge, which are constructed from square-planer [Ni(CN)(4)](2-).

a new cyanide-bridge Cu(II)- Ni(II) coordination polymer with a two-dimensional grid-type structure, and it is the first example of a square-planar [M(CN)(4)](2-) anion (M = Ni) with a 4,4'-bipyridine ligand in its crystal structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work is the first report on a cyanide-bridging heterometallic system constructed from the square-planar [Cu(H2)O2](2+) cation and the anionic [Ni (CN)4](2) unit.
a new cyanide-bridge heterometallic Cu(II)- Ni(II) compound has been successfully prepared and its structural, thermal, spectroscopic, and magnetic properties have been investigated.
the Cu(2+) and Ni(2+) ions are connected by bridging cyanide groups to generate a two-dimensional grid network, which further expands into a three-dimensional structure by O-H...N hydrogen bonding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present study provides a new insight into the synthesis and characterization of a novel heterometallic cyanide-bridging compound.
this new compound is a new example of a two-dimensional coordination polymer constructed from a square-planar [M(CN)(4)](2-) (M = Ni, P = 2) ion and a monovalent cationic unit.
the [Cu(H2)O]n(2+) units in the crystal lattice are connected to the [Ni(CN)](n)2- units by bridging cyanide groups, which results in the formation of a two-dimensional grid-type structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the [Ni(CN)](4)(2-) anion can act as a good bridging group for Cu(II) ions.
the [Cu(II)2Ni(II)(H2O)4(CN)6]2+ cationic unit is a good precursor for the construction of heterometallic complexes with different metal cations.
the [Cu(II) Ni(II) (CN)4(H 2O)2 ]·H 2O system can be used as a building block for a wide range of supramolecular structures with interesting magnetic, electrical and catalytic properties.
